decisionsTitle: The facelift, phase 1: the pink pair, Inter 800, «Aspectul nou» and the public shell (amending §692, §460, §262, §569, §699)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-11:** phase 1 of the facelift starts with the plan's defaults (`docs/REDESIGN.md`, §692). That takes decisions 1 (the pink beside the logo blue), 2 (Inter 800 for headings) and 12 (one setting, «Aspectul nou», off on production until the club approves on QA) by their defaults. His standing rules of 2026-10-10 apply: component-based, easy for whoever vibe-codes next, one design system the pages stay consistent with — every new primitive drawn on `/admin/design` with its names and tokens.

**Decision — the tokens.** `src/theme/brand.ts` gains eight colours in `COLOR`, each with a twin in `COLOR_DARK`: `accent` (the hot pink, for the mark, a rule or a large word), `accentInk` (the pink that carries words: `primary` under the new look, the plan's «pinkInk»), `accentDeep` (a contained pink button under the pointer), `accentTint` (a pale pink band), `kindSpecial` and `kindSpecialInk` (a special event's green, for phase 4), `kindOther` (a warm grey) and `inkStrong` (headings). `brand-pairs.ts` adds `LOOK_PAIRS` and `LOOK_PAIRS_DARK`, seventeen pairs a scheme, and `tests/unit/theme/brand.test.ts` holds every one at AA (4.5 : 1). One more rule is asserted rather than assumed: `accentInk` is no lighter than `inkMuted`. §488 already holds `inkMuted` at AA on every page tint the club may choose, a typed one included, so the pink link holds there too. The design page draws the new swatches and both pair tables from the same constants.

**Decision — Inter 800.** `src/theme/fonts/Inter-800.woff2` is Google's own file, from the same release and the same request as the three Inter files already in the repository: Inter v20, latin and latin-ext in one WOFF2, fetched with §460's recipe. Inter 700 fetched the same way is byte-identical to the file in the repository. The layout adds it to the `--font-inter` family, not preloaded. Only the new look's scope names the face (`FONT.lookDisplay`), so with the setting off no browser fetches it. With it on, the headings swap in when the file lands, instead of every visitor of every page paying 52 KB for a look that may be off. §460's face list now names Inter 800 as a heading face, not preloaded (BR-REQ-101-01 criterion 10: every font is a repository file). `h1`–`h3` take it at 800 with `letter-spacing: -0.02em`. The body stays Roboto.

**Decision — the scope.** `src/theme/look.ts` names where the new look applies. The locale layout sets `data-look="2026"` on `<html>` while the setting is on, the way MUI's `data-dark` switches the scheme (§93), and every new-look rule is a plain-object selector under `UNDER_LOOK`: `html[data-look="2026"]:not(:has([data-backoffice])) &`, plus the design page's preview box. The backoffice shares the layout and the header, but its shell carries the marker the tint and the text size already stop at (§488, §530), so staff never see the new look. A browser without `:has()` shows today's look. The rules are: MUI buttons become pills (theme override); `h1`–`h3` in Inter 800 (theme override); the pressed button's blue gradient (`accentOnHover`, §166) gives way to MUI's own hover under the scope, so the gradient budget stays three; and the logo is drawn in ink. The logo uses `grayscale(1)` on the supplied lockup, which turns its pure blue into a near-black within a step of `inkStrong` and keeps its light-grey strokes, where a one-colour mask would flatten them. The file is untouched. A theme override sits below a component's own `sx`, so a page that states its own radius or weight keeps it: the look changes the defaults, never a choice.

**Decision — the pink `primary`.** MUI's own `--mui-palette-primary-*` variables (main `accentInk`, light `accent`, dark `accentDeep`, the words on the fill white by day and the dark page after dark), and their `…Channel` twins, are redefined under the scope by one small unlayered stylesheet the layout draws (`siteLookStyle`). That is the tint's mechanism (§488). It cannot be a theme override: MUI emits its variables in its CSS layer above the global sublayer, where an override would lose whatever its specificity. A test pins the variable names against `theme.vars`. Every value is a `brand.ts` token. The emails, the PDFs, the race numbers and the share cards never read it.

**Decision — the setting.** «Setări» → «Aspect» → «Aspectul nou» is a third card beside the tint and the text size, with the same shape: two radios («Aspectul de azi», the default, and «Aspectul nou»), Save behind the §384 question, the Administrator's alone (`canManageClubSettings`, asserted at the page, the action and the service), audited as `site_look.changed` under its own entity id, and stored as one `platform_settings` row (`siteLook`, `{ on }`) with no migration (§100). A save expires the public cache's settings, so every static page is made again in the look now in force (§549). The layout and the header read it through the public cache with the last good copy behind it (§447), so an outage shows today's look. With no row, the layout and the header read the setting and draw nothing new: no attribute, no stylesheet, no button, no watermark. The card's button «Vezi-le una lângă alta» opens the design page.

**Decision — the shell.** Under the new look the header carries «Vino cu noi» / "Join us", a pink pill with a trailing arrow. It leads to the next weekly run's page, or to the listing when none is ahead (decision 5). The next weekly run is the soonest date, still going ahead, of a series that recurs every week, recognised as the listing recognises a series (`nextWeeklyRun`, from the listing's own cached read: no query of its own, and the page is held no longer than the listing's clock window). The button and the socials are the nav's children, drawn into its trailing group inside `SiteNav` before the ☰, so the ☰ stays the row's right edge (§699) and the nav's own measurement subtracts their room before it folds a section (§262, §569). On a phone the button keeps its arrow (§521) in a tighter pill (less padding, a 16-pixel arrow, a smaller gap), so the row stays one row at 320 pixels with the logo, «Alergări» and the ☰. The two social marks, Facebook and Instagram from the footer's one list (§565), show from `md`; below that the footer's bar carries them. The mountain mark, an inline SVG of a few hundred bytes in `currentColor`, sits faint at the foot of every public page as the shell's watermark. All of these are drawn only inside the scope, so a backoffice page, which renders in the same header and layout, never shows them. `HeaderCta` and `HeaderSocials` take no `order` of their own: where they sit is the nav's. The new primitives are `ArrowButtonLink` (words first, then the arrow, 44 pixels, `contained` pink or `outlined` ink; the arrow its one icon file as the last child, never `endIcon`, §370), `HeaderCta`, `HeaderSocials`, `MountainMark` and `LookWatermark`, all Server Components. The header gains no new client component: the button is the house `ButtonLink`. The cost the owner watches: with the setting on, every public page's header reads the listing's cached upcoming events (`cachedUpcomingEvents`), which carries the `events` tag and holds the static page no longer than the next event's end, so a static page (legal, gallery, «Echipa») is made again on every event write and at each event's end, a little more often than today; off, the header reads nothing more.

**Decision — the design page.** `/admin/design` opens on «Aspectul nou»: today's look and the new one side by side, drawn by the same components. The right-hand box carries `data-look-preview="2026"`, which every new-look rule also reads, and the page draws the same palette stylesheet for it, so the page shows the rules themselves rather than a copy. Under that come the table of MUI's primary onto the pink tokens (light and dark) and the mountain mark at three sizes. The Colours section adds the new swatches and the two pair tables; the Type section adds the Inter 800 face and the role `lookDisplay`; Rules gains «newLook». The plan's data (`redesign-plan.ts`) marks decisions 1, 2 and 12 `decided` and phase 1 `building`. `docs/REDESIGN.md` says the same and lists where each part lives (§ Phase 1, as built), and `docs/VIBECODING.md` → «Where things live» has a row for the facelift.

**Refused:** a `--br-…` variable family of our own that the theme would read (MUI's own variables are what every component already paints with, and the tint set the precedent); `theme.applyStyles` or a second theme for the public pages (a function cannot cross into a client component, and two themes are two things to keep in step); reading the setting in a page or a component to branch its markup (a rule under the scope is the one way, so the old look is deleted later by deleting rules); preloading Inter 800 (52 KB on every page for a look that is off); a heading colour override (it would outrank a page's own `color` on a canvas such as «Echipa»'s, §701, so `inkStrong` is a token for the components that ask for it); the arrow on every button (it marks a way on, not a save); a custom mask or a redrawn logo for the ink logo (the club's artwork stays the file it supplied).

**Turning it on, on QA:** the default is off everywhere, so the one click is «Setări» → «Aspect» → «Aspectul nou» → choose «Aspectul nou» → «Salvează aspectul» → confirm (an Administrator); decision 12's «pornită pe QA» means that click. **The gate:** `tests/e2e/header-nav.spec.ts` flips the setting through that screen and measures the header at 320 pixels (one row, «Alergări» on it, the arrow kept, the button before the ☰ and the ☰ at the right edge, no sideways overflow), and a render test (`tests/unit/appearance/site-look-header.test.ts`) holds that off the header is the same markup with no button, socials or watermark and on it leads to the weekly run or the listing. Phase 1's gate is also the club's yes on QA with the setting on, on a phone and a laptop. **Browsers without `:has()`** drop the whole new-look rule, the design page's preview box included, which is the safe side.
changelogLine: - **«Aspectul nou» (off until the club says yes on QA)** — a switch under «Setări» → «Aspect» that dresses the public pages in the facelift's first layer: a pink primary beside the logo blue, Inter 800 headings, pill buttons, «Vino cu noi» to the next weekly run in the header with Facebook and Instagram, the logo in ink and a mountain mark at the foot of the page; the backoffice, emails and PDFs never change, and `/admin/design` shows both looks side by side. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Only an Administrator (canManageClubSettings) saves «Aspectul nou», asserted at the page, the action and the service; a save is audited as site_look.changed under the setting's own entity id and expires the public cache's settings, and a refused save writes and expires nothing (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Every token of the new look has a dark twin, every text/background pair it draws clears WCAG AA in both schemes, and the pink that carries words is no lighter than the muted ink, so it clears AA on every page tint the club may choose (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

With «Aspectul nou» off no page carries the look's attribute, stylesheet, header button, social marks or watermark; with it on they are drawn only on the public pages, never inside the backoffice shell, «Vino cu noi» keeps its arrow on a phone and sits before the ☰, which stays the row's right edge, and it leads to the soonest going-ahead date of a weekly series, else to the listing (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
Inter 800, the heading face of «Aspectul nou», is a file in the repository and is not preloaded, so with the setting off no browser fetches it (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
